finding.title: Metrics label cardinality is unbounded and fed by the client-controlled model field on request paths that run before rate limiting
finding.evidence: metrics.go:56-63 'func (mt *Metrics) Observe(model string, isErr bool) {' ... 's := mt.stats[model]' / 'if s == nil {' / 's = &ModelStat{lastSec: now}' / 'mt.stats[model] = s' — the map key is the request's model string, with no key cap, no length cap and no eviction anywhere (ModelStat is 'buckets [60]int64' + 'errs [60]int64' = 960 B per key, metrics.go:10-14; searching the whole backend for delete-on-stats returns only these two assignment sites). The key is attacker-chosen: gateway.go:334 'ap.alias = cr.Model' is assigned immediately after parsing, before every validation branch, and gateway.go:314-319 'defer func() {' ... 's.mx.Observe(ap.alias, ap.status != "ok")' records it even when the request is rejected — including unknown models (gateway.go:356-361) and denied models (gateway.go:370-376), both of which return before the limiter at gateway.go:410 'if ok2, hit := s.rl.Allow(snap, apiKey.ID, ap.alias); !ok2 {'. cr.Model has no length bound (adapter/adapter.go:108 'Model string `json:"model"`' with only the empty check at adapter.go:120-122 'if raw.Model == "" {' / 'return nil, fmt.Errorf("model is required")' / '}'); the only ceiling is the 16 MiB body read at gateway.go:322. Every accumulated key is then re-emitted verbatim to unauthenticated readers: metrics/prom.go:135-138 'for _, q := range qps {' / 'l := ...promEsc(q.Model)...' / 'writeMetric(w, "gw_model_requests_per_second", "Per-model requests per second (60s window)", l, q.QPS)'.

reason: VERIFIED LINE-BY-LINE (every quote read in place; file+line exact, so the primary evidence is not a misquote and the chain does not break). metrics.go:56 'func (mt *Metrics) Observe(model string, isErr bool) {', :60 's := mt.stats[model]', :61 'if s == nil {', :62 's = &ModelStat{lastSec: now}', :63 'mt.stats[model] = s' — all verbatim; line 63 is the unbounded insertion site, so the reported anchor is correct. metrics.go:10-14 'type ModelStat struct { buckets [60]int64 / errs [60]int64 / lastSec int64 }' = 968 B, which Go allocates in the 1024-byte size class => ~1 KB per new key plus the retained key string. No eviction exists anywhere: grep of the whole backend for 'delete(' hits only audit/hub.go:41 and slb/slb.go:215 (never mt.stats); the Metrics type exposes exactly Observe/RecordError/QPS/RecentErrors/ConnInc/ConnDec/Conns/Uptime/WritePromRender — there is no reset, prune, cap, TTL or LRU method; and metrics.New() is called exactly once for the process (cmd/server/main.go:65; the only other hit is gateway_test.go:25), so even a config hot-reload/rebuild of the runtime snapshot does not recreate the map. Only a process restart reclaims it. The map key is attacker-controlled and recorded pre-authorisation: gateway.go:334 'ap.alias = cr.Model' is set immediately after ParseRequest and before every validation branch, and gateway.go:314-319 is 'defer func() { if shouldAuditCall(...) { s.writeLog(ap) }; s.mx.Observe(ap.alias, ap.status != "ok") }()' — a deferred write on every exit path. The unknown-model path gateway.go:356-361 ('if !ok {' / 'ap.errMsg = "unknown model alias: " + cr.Model' / clientError 404 / 'return') and the denied-model path gateway.go:370-376 ('if !apiKey.AllowsModel(cr.Model) {' / clientError 403 / 'return') both return before the limiter at gateway.go:410 'if ok2, hit := s.rl.Allow(snap, apiKey.ID, ap.alias); !ok2 {' and before the quota check at gateway.go:419, so neither rate limit nor quota can ever shed this load. cr.Model has no length or charset bound: adapter/adapter.go:108 'Model string `json:"model"`' inside the anonymous struct unmarshalled at :117, with the only validation being adapter.go:120-122 'if raw.Model == "" { return nil, fmt.Errorf("model is required") }'; encoding/json imposes no per-field limit, so the sole ceiling is gateway.go:322 'body, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(c.Request.Body, 16<<20))' — a ~16 MiB model name is legal, and json.Unmarshal allocates a fresh string for it, which the map key then pins permanently. Emission to unauthenticated readers is confirmed: admin/routes.go:21-24 registers 'r.GET("/metrics", ...)' with 's.mx.WritePromRender(c.Writer, s)' and the comment at :19-20 states outright that JWT auth is deliberately omitted ('故不做 JWT 鉴权'); prom.go:135-138 emits 'l := `model="` + promEsc(q.Model) + `"`' and then two samples per key ('gw_model_requests_per_second' at :137 and 'gw_model_errors_1m' at :138). I also closed a gap the original did not check: the collector path cannot cap the list either — admin/prom.go:15 'snap.ModelQPS = s.mx.QPS()', so the prom.go:121-123 fallback ('if qps == nil { qps = mt.QPS() }') and the collector path are equivalent, and QPS() (metrics.go:88-103) appends every key unconditionally, with no filter for keys whose 60-second windows are all zero, so an entry is emitted forever once created. Three corrections that do NOT refute the finding: (a) the evidence overstates the 403 branch — reaching gateway.go:370 requires cr.Model to have already resolved at gateway.go:335 ('ups, ok := snap.Aliases[cr.Model]') or :351 ('if iups := snap.UpstreamModels[cr.Model]'), i.e. a name in the admin-defined set, so the denied-model path adds only bounded keys; the 404 unknown-model path alone is sufficient and unbounded, so the impact claim stands. (b) The 'adjacent' call_logs note understates a mitigation: audit.go:88-106 cleanupLoop runs hourly and does 'l.db.Where("created_at < ?", cutoff).Delete(&model.CallLog{})' at AuditRetentionDays (settings.go:31 default 90), so DB growth is bounded by retention x rate rather than literally unbounded — but this asymmetry strengthens the core claim, since the metrics map has no reclaim path at all. (c) 'two assignment sites' is loose (there is one write site, metrics.go:63; the only production Observe call site is gateway.go:318). Mitigations I independently checked and found not to break the chain: AuthMiddleware does run first (gateway.go:215-221 key lookup, :222 IP allow), so this needs a valid API key — that is why severity is authed-but-severe (high) and not critical; MaxConnections at gateway.go:195-200 bounds only concurrent in-flight /v1 requests (and does not cover /metrics at all, which also has no connection cap) and nothing about retained map entries; promEsc (prom.go:43-45) prevents label/newline injection into the exposition text but does nothing about cardinality; and RecordError is explicitly capped at 50 events (metrics.go:77-79), proving the codebase bounds its other unbounded structures while leaving stats unbounded. There is no global middleware in front of Handle that could limit this: main.go:89-118 installs only gin.Recovery, security headers and an access logger, with no gin.BodyLimit, no per-IP limiter and no MaxHeaderBytes tuning. Consequence: per-tenant memory is monotonic for process lifetime and ends in OOM of the single-node gateway (all tenants down); each probe is additionally converted into permanent per-scrape CPU and response bytes on the unauthenticated monitoring path (QPS() holds mt.mu across the full O(N) rotate+sort, so that cost is also amplified onto the gateway hot path via Observe), and tenant A's probed model names become permanently visible in the label set to every anonymous reader of /metrics.
exploit_sketch: Prerequisite: one valid gateway API key (any low-privilege tenant, sk-... from the admin console; the key need not be allowed any model). 1) Loop POST /v1/chat/completions with Authorization: Bearer sk-... and a body of {"model":"x-<uniq>-<n>","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}. The name resolves to no alias (gateway.go:335) and no implicit upstream (gateway.go:351), so the handler takes gateway.go:356-361 and returns 404 — without ever touching the rate limiter at gateway.go:410 or the quota manager at gateway.go:419. 2) The deferred block at gateway.go:314-319 still runs s.mx.Observe(ap.alias, true) with ap.alias == the attacker's string (set at gateway.go:334), inserting a new never-freed ~1 KB entry into mt.stats at metrics.go:63. At 100 unique names/s that is ~100 KB/s ≈ 8.6 GB/day retained; nothing in the process ever deletes a stats key, so growth is monotonic to OOM, taking the single-node gateway down for every tenant. 3) Amplify per-request by making the model value huge instead of numerous: the same 404 path pins up to ~16 MiB per request (only limit: io.LimitReader of 16<<20 at gateway.go:322; no length check in adapter.go:108/120-122), so a few hundred requests retain gigabytes. 4) Monitoring-path DoS + cross-tenant disclosure, no credentials needed for this leg: GET /metrics (unauthenticated by design, routes.go:19-24) now returns gw_model_requests_per_second / gw_model_errors_1m lines for every name ever probed — megabytes per scrape, serialised behind metrics.promMu (prom.go:113), with entries never ageing out because QPS() emits zero-QPS keys too — so N transient authenticated probes become permanent anonymous bandwidth/CPU cost, and every tenant sees every other tenant's probed model names.
